title: compare a replacement mainframe transaction with the original workload
input: The modernization team selects representative transactions and permitted comparison datasets.
action: Dual Run supports parallel validation of the selected original and replacement processing outcomes. The configured comparison identifies differences; the team determines whether they represent valid changes or migration defects.
output: The migration owner resolves unexplained differences before allowing the replacement to serve production transactions.
check: Test representative business cases, state isolation, output comparison and final cutover conditions.

title: reconcile enterprise entities into an accepted relationship graph
input: The data owner supplies approved entity records and source identifiers from multiple systems.
action: Enterprise Knowledge Graph's supported entity-reconciliation workflow links or enriches entity information according to its configuration. The analyst validates uncertain matches and preserves source evidence before trusting graph relationships.
output: The application uses the accepted entity identifiers and relationships for authorized search or analysis.
check: Check false merges, source provenance, update handling and access restrictions before publishing reconciled entities.

title: persist application documents through the compatible database interface
input: The backend submits validated document writes using a supported MongoDB-compatible driver and command set.
action: The selected Firestore MongoDB-compatible offering stores documents and executes its supported operations. Compatibility limits, indexing and transaction behavior must match the actual application rather than every MongoDB assumption.
output: The backend returns the accepted record and reads it using the caller's permitted application scope.
check: Test driver support, query plans, conflicting writes and retry semantics against the exact configured offering.

title: assess a sensitive customer action before applying a risk policy
input: The application collects the supported client token and permitted login or transaction context.
action: The configured reCAPTCHA or Fraud Defense assessment analyzes the submitted interaction and returns supported risk evidence. The backend validates token properties and applies its own allow, challenge or review policy.
output: The application executes only the action allowed by the accepted risk and business authorization checks.
check: Test invalid tokens, action mismatch, false positives and provider failure without allowing risk scores to replace user authorization.

title: operate supported Kubernetes clusters across configured cloud environments
input: The platform owner selects supported cluster providers, versions and fleet requirements.
action: GKE Multi-Cloud's selected offering manages supported Kubernetes cluster operations across the configured provider environments. Cluster workers execute pods; provider networking, identities and lifecycle constraints remain explicit.
output: The application team deploys the accepted workload to the chosen member cluster and verifies its dependencies.
check: Check current provider support, upgrade behavior, fleet permissions and cross-cloud dependency failures before rollout.

title: release an enterprise agent with authorized tools and evaluated behavior
input: The team defines the agent task, permitted sources, model configuration and action boundaries.
action: The selected agent platform supplies supported agent development, runtime or management capabilities. Agent code and configured tools perform the task; enterprise identity and tool policy limit the accessible data and actions.
output: The application presents the accepted answer and requires approval for consequential actions according to its policy.
check: Test source access, tool denial, prompt injection and evaluation regressions before promoting the agent version.

title: investigate a correlated security detection before containment
input: The security team configures approved log ingestion, normalization and detection scope.
action: Google SecOps ingests supported security evidence and evaluates configured detections or investigation queries. A detection identifies relevant activity; authorized playbooks or responders perform the actual containment through connected tools.
output: The analyst validates affected identities and assets and applies the approved response action.
check: Check ingestion gaps, detection evidence, playbook permissions and actual containment results before closing the case.

title: prepare an authorized clinical dataset for healthcare analysis
input: The healthcare owner selects supported clinical sources and the permitted analytical scope.
action: Healthcare Data Engine's supported integrations prepare and harmonize clinical data according to its configured workflow. Patient identifiers, terminology and source mappings need clinical validation before analytical consumption.
output: The authorized clinical analytics application queries the accepted harmonized dataset.
check: Reconcile clinical events, source completeness, terminology mappings and patient-data access before trusting analytical results.

title: perform an authorized ERP lookup through a configured connector
input: The integration backend submits the permitted customer identifier and selected ERP operation.
action: Integration Connectors provides the supported connection and operation interface to the configured external system. The ERP executes the requested lookup under the connector's credentials; field mappings and permissions limit exposed data.
output: The integration returns only the validated permitted fields to the requesting application.
check: Test connector scope, credential expiry, schema changes and denied-record access before exposing the lookup.

title: discover a governed dataset and request its actual source access
input: The data steward registers supported assets, ownership and metadata collection scope.
action: Knowledge Catalog's supported catalog capabilities organize data or knowledge assets and relevant metadata. Discovery and classification help users find sources; actual dataset access is enforced through the configured underlying resource permissions.
output: The analyst identifies the correct asset and requests the permitted access from its owner.
check: Check metadata freshness, source links, classification accuracy and denied-data access before accepting catalog coverage.
